_about: FLAMEPRINT seed catalog (24 investigations). Investigation-level metadata curated from the NASA Space Apps 2026 'Flame in Freefall' challenge brief, the NASA Researcher's Guide to ISS Combustion Science (2015, data/psi/docs), and the NASA Glenn combustion science page. It contains NO test-level measurements. Condition envelopes marked 'approx' are coarse orientation ranges that must be verified against PSI; null means 'not characterized here' (design/apparatus ranges are kept in 'note', never claimed as coverage). Importing PSI test files (data/psi or the Data Lab) replaces envelopes with values derived from real test records. Any investigation can be overridden by importing a JSON object with the same id.

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
investigations.geometry: Small flat samples, rods/cylinders and spheres in a fan-driven low-speed flow duct
investigations.objective: Observe ignition, flame spread and extinction of solid materials in low-speed flow in microgravity, and how flames respond to reduced flow and suppressant.

conditions.note: Cabin-air MSG environment; flow varied by the duct fan. Coarse envelope: verify against PSI.

insights.prevention: Solids in microgravity can keep burning in low-speed flows that never occur on Earth, so cabin ventilation speed directly affects material flammability.
insights.suppression: Cutting the flow, or adding suppressant, can put out solid flames. The response depends on sample geometry and flow speed.
insights.modeling: Flame-spread and extinction data across flat, cylindrical and spherical samples, for validating spread models.

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids – II
investigations.geometry: Flat, cylindrical and spherical solid samples in a fan-driven low-speed flow duct
investigations.objective: Extend BASS by varying oxygen concentration (nitrogen dilution) and flow speed to map flammability limits of solids in microgravity.

conditions.note: Reduced-O2 tests by nitrogen dilution. Coarse envelope: exact test matrix in PSI.

insights.prevention: Maps the limiting oxygen concentration for solids against flow speed in microgravity, which is the core input for accepting materials in a new atmosphere.
insights.modeling: Oxygen and flow flammability boundaries, suitable for calibrating predictive flammability models.
insights.general: Tests whether normal-gravity material screening remains conservative under microgravity conditions.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration – I
investigations.geometry: Large fabric sheet in forced flow
investigations.objective: Observe large-scale fire growth over a spacecraft material in microgravity, at a scale impossible to test safely aboard a crewed vehicle.

conditions.note: Vehicle cabin air with low forced flow. Coarse envelope.

insights.prevention: Large-scale flame spread over a fabric in microgravity, showing the size and growth a real spacecraft fire could reach.
insights.detection: Recorded how a large fire changes cabin pressure, temperature and gas composition, which matters for detector placement and alarm thresholds.
insights.modeling: A scale-up benchmark for whole-vehicle fire models.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration – II
investigations.geometry: Several smaller material samples burned in sequence
investigations.objective: Measure ignition and flammability of a set of different spacecraft materials in microgravity.

insights.prevention: Compares several real spacecraft materials under the same microgravity conditions, so they can be ranked against each other for material selection.
insights.detection: Recorded fire signatures of several materials in a spacecraft-scale volume.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration – III
investigations.geometry: Large fabric sheet in forced flow (repeat and extension of Saffire-I)
investigations.objective: Repeat and extend large-scale microgravity flame spread to build confidence in fire-growth and spacecraft-response data.

insights.detection: Repeat large-scale fire data, so detection and cabin-response measurements can be checked for repeatability.
insights.modeling: A second large-scale benchmark for whole-vehicle fire models.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
investigations.geometry: Free-floating or tethered spherical fuel droplets (millimetre scale)
investigations.objective: Test how well gaseous suppressants (dilution with carbon dioxide and helium) put out burning fuel droplets in microgravity.

conditions.note: Quiescent chamber; O2, pressure and CO2/He dilution varied. Import the PSI test matrix for exact values.

insights.suppression: Measured how much CO2 or helium dilution it takes to put out droplet flames, which directly informs suppressant choice and post-fire atmospheres. Key finding (NASA Researcher's Guide, 2015): the flammability limit is LOWER in reduced gravity, so terrestrial inert-gas suppressant standards do not offer the same margin of safety in low gravity as on Earth.
insights.general: Large n-heptane droplets kept burning after the visible flame went out, through a low-temperature 'cool flame'. MDCA supports droplets 1-5 mm in a 0-3 atm ambient of up to 40% O2 (balance inert).
insights.detection: Burning can continue with no visible flame, so optical flame detection alone can miss it.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment – 2
investigations.geometry: Single droplets and droplet arrays, some with slow convective flow
investigations.objective: Study burning rates, soot formation and extinction of single- and multi-component fuel droplets, including the effect of slow flow.

conditions.note: Import the PSI test matrix for exact values.

insights.suppression: Extinction behaviour of fuel mixtures, relevant to liquid spills and leaks.
insights.modeling: Droplet burning-rate and soot data for validating models of multi-component fuels.

investigations.name: Cool Flames Investigation
investigations.geometry: Spherical fuel droplets
investigations.objective: Characterize low-temperature 'cool flame' droplet combustion, first observed in FLEX, across fuels, pressures and oxygen levels.

conditions.note: Includes elevated pressures. Import the PSI test matrix for exact values.

insights.detection: Cool flames are nearly invisible and produce different products from hot flames, so detection strategies need to account for them.
insights.modeling: Low-temperature chemistry data for validating kinetic models.

investigations.name: Burning Rate Emulator (ACME)
investigations.geometry: Porous burner surface emulating a burning solid or liquid
investigations.objective: Use gaseous fuels to emulate burning solids and liquids, and find flammability in still atmospheres as a function of material properties.

conditions.note: Still (quiescent) atmospheres; import the PSI test matrix for O2 and pressure.

insights.prevention: Relates still-air flammability to material properties, so new materials can be assessed without burning every one.
insights.modeling: Property-based flammability correlations for predictive models.

investigations.name: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (ACME)
fuels: flammable gas (e.g., propane) mixed with nitrogen in the chamber
investigations.geometry: Inside-out spherical flames: an O2/N2 mixture flows out of a spherical burner into a fuel/N2 chamber
investigations.objective: Study gaseous cool flames. These include the highest-oxygen microgravity tests in PSI, with an oxidizer stream of up to 85% O2.

conditions.note: 85% is the challenge-stated maximum of the burner OXIDIZER stream, not ambient O2. Lower bound is a placeholder.

insights.prevention: The only microgravity data in PSI at or above Moon-base oxygen levels (30% or more). It is an inverse gaseous flame, not a burning solid.

investigations.name: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (ACME)
investigations.geometry: Laminar diffusion flames with an applied electric field
investigations.objective: Study how electric fields act on the ions in flames. The resulting body force mimics partial gravity.

insights.general: The only partial-gravity proxy in PSI: an electric body force on flame ions acts like adjustable gravity.
insights.modeling: Lets models be tested between 0 g and 1 g before LUCI and FM2 data exist.

investigations.name: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (ACME)
investigations.geometry: Axisymmetric coflow jet flames
investigations.objective: Measure the structure, soot and stability of laminar coflow diffusion flames in microgravity.

insights.detection: Without buoyancy, soot forms differently, which changes the smoke that detectors rely on.
insights.modeling: Benchmark flames for detailed soot and flame-structure models.

investigations.name: Flame Design (ACME)
fuels: gaseous fuels with inert dilution (normal and inverse flames)
investigations.geometry: Spherical diffusion flames
investigations.objective: Learn how flame structure (normal vs. inverse, dilution) controls soot, to design soot-free, robust flames.

insights.detection: Relates flame structure to soot (smoke) production.
insights.modeling: Spherical flames are effectively 1-D, which makes them clean model-validation cases.

investigations.name: Structure & Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (ACME)
investigations.geometry: Spherical diffusion flames
investigations.objective: Measure the growth, structure and extinction of spherical diffusion flames for comparison with models.

insights.suppression: Extinction limits of diffusion flames caused by radiation and dilution.
insights.modeling: Transient spherical flames as model-validation targets.

investigations.name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
investigations.geometry: Laminar jet diffusion flames in co-flowing air
investigations.objective: Find the smoke points (the onset of soot emission) of gas-jet flames in microgravity.

insights.detection: Shows when microgravity flames start emitting smoke, the signal smoke detectors rely on.
insights.modeling: Soot-emission criteria for radiation and smoke models.

investigations.name: Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
investigations.geometry: Lifted and attached jet diffusion flames in co-flow
investigations.objective: Study flame liftoff and blowout of jet flames in microgravity.

insights.suppression: Liftoff and blowout limits show when flow alone can detach or extinguish a gas flame, such as one fed by a leak.

investigations.name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
investigations.geometry: Small material samples heated to produce smoke (non-flaming)
investigations.objective: Measure smoke particle size from overheated spacecraft materials to improve smoke-detector design.

conditions.note: Pyrolysis smoke in cabin air. Coarse envelope.

insights.detection: Smoke made in microgravity can differ from ground-test smoke, which affects detector response. This is the basis for detector design.
insights.general: Early-warning detection aims at overheating (pyrolysis) before any open flame.

investigations.name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment – Refurbished
investigations.geometry: Small heated samples producing smoke
investigations.objective: Extend SAME smoke characterization with more materials and conditions to support detector design.

insights.detection: Adds materials and repeat data to the smoke database used to set detector thresholds.

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
investigations.geometry: Cabin aerosol sampling
investigations.objective: Test whether a particle instrument used for SAME smoke studies can measure cabin dust.

insights.detection: Cabin dust is background noise for smoke detectors. Knowing its level helps avoid false alarms, which will matter with lunar dust.

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test – 2
investigations.geometry: Cabin aerosol sampling
investigations.objective: Follow-on dust-measurement feasibility test.

insights.detection: More background-aerosol data, relevant to smoke-detector false-alarm rates.

investigations.name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction
investigations.apparatus: SoFIE flow duct (larger, improved BASS-concept duct)
fuels: representative thick and thin solid fuels
investigations.geometry: Forced opposed-flow flame spread over solid samples in a flow duct
investigations.objective: Find the fundamental limiting oxygen concentration for solid materials in microgravity, as a function of forced opposed flow velocity, ambient oxygen concentration and pressure, and test whether the NASA-STD-6001 1 g flame-propagation acceptance test is conservative in low gravity.

conditions.note: DESIGN range per the NASA Researcher's Guide (2015): oxygen 10-40% by volume, pressure 0.2-1.5 atm (~20-152 kPa), forced opposed flow. This is the apparatus/planned range, NOT verified PSI coverage — left null so it does not over-claim. Import the PSI test matrix to characterize.

insights.prevention: SoFIE directly tests whether ground-based material acceptance (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1, a 1 g upward flame-spread test) stays conservative in microgravity, where some materials are flammable at lower oxygen than on Earth.
insights.modeling: Limiting-oxygen-vs-flow data across thick and thin solids for calibrating microgravity flammability models; successor to the BASS flow-duct approach.

investigations.provenance: NASA Researcher's Guide to ISS Combustion Science (2015) + NASA Glenn combustion science page (retrieved 2026-11-14). PSI presence/records not verified locally.

investigations.name: Flammability Limits At Reduced-g Experiment
investigations.geometry: Flame spread over solid samples, compared between normal gravity and microgravity
investigations.objective: Estimate microgravity material flammability limits from ground-based data by comparing normal-gravity and microgravity flame spread, to provide a practical screening method for material acceptance.

conditions.note: International collaboration (JAXA, NASA, ESA, CNES, DLR and universities). Conditions not characterized in public summaries; import the PSI test matrix.

measurements: flammability limit estimate (1 g vs microgravity)

insights.prevention: Aims to let ground tests predict microgravity flammability, which would make material screening cheaper and faster if validated.
insights.general: A NASA/JAXA/ESA/CNES/DLR collaboration bridging normal-gravity and microgravity flammability.

investigations.provenance: NASA Glenn combustion science page (retrieved 2026-11-14). PSI presence/records not verified locally.

investigations.name: Lunar-g Combustion Investigation (expected)
investigations.geometry: TBD
investigations.objective: Expected partial-gravity combustion data. Not yet in PSI.

insights.general: Expected to fill the partial-gravity gap. FLAMEPRINT will use it automatically once its data are imported.

investigations.name: Flammability of Materials on the Moon (FM2)
investigations.platform: Lunar surface — lunar gravity (1/6 g, ~0.165 g)
investigations.geometry: Flame spread over a fabric sample in lunar gravity
investigations.objective: Burn a material on the Moon's surface to obtain the first combustion data at lunar gravity (1/6 g), filling the partial-gravity gap between microgravity and 1 g. Ground-simulated beforehand in a drop-tower centrifuge. Data not yet in PSI.

conditions.note: Lunar gravity (1/6 g). Exact atmosphere and flow TBD; no data in PSI yet. Design range is the acceptance question FLAMEPRINT scores for the Moon base.

insights.general: Described by NASA Glenn as the first combustion experiment on another planetary body (the Moon). Expected to give lunar-gravity material flammability data directly, which no microgravity experiment can.

investigations.provenance: NASA Glenn combustion science page (nasa.gov/glenn, retrieved 2026-11-14) + challenge brief

relations.note: E-field body force mimics partial g
SoFIE uses a larger, improved flow duct along the BASS concept
μg limiting-oxygen data informs lunar-g material acceptance
Flammability limits: μg experiments inform the 1 g→μg estimation method

earthSpinoffs.title: Fine-water-mist extinguishers
earthSpinoffs.text: Fine-water-mist extinguishers developed for the ISS have practical uses on Earth.

earthSpinoffs.title: Smoke detection
earthSpinoffs.text: NASA technology has led to improvements in smoke detection on Earth. Microgravity smoke-particle data inform detector design.

earthSpinoffs.title: Firefighter gear
earthSpinoffs.text: NASA technology has improved firefighter protective clothing and air tanks.

earthSpinoffs.title: Material flammability testing
earthSpinoffs.text: Microgravity flammability limits test whether ground-based material screening is conservative, which helps flammability testing on Earth too.

earthSpinoffs.title: Cleaner combustion
earthSpinoffs.text: Cool-flame and soot chemistry measured without buoyancy feed combustion models used for engines and burners.

earthSpinoffs.title: Fire safety in confined spaces
earthSpinoffs.text: Saffire grew large fires inside a closed, ventilated cargo module, and SAME characterized smoke without buoyancy. Both bear on places people cannot quickly leave, such as submarines, aircraft cabins and mines.
